posts.title: Wooden posts and split boards survive 10,500 years beneath a German lake
posts.dek: Divers recovered worked timbers from 20 metres down in Lake Arendsee. The pieces show felling marks and could rewrite what we know about hunter-gatherer building.

posts.title: 10,500-year-old wooden posts found beneath german lake
posts.dek: Divers recovered split boards and a tall post from lake arendsee, where waterlogged conditions have preserved stone-age timbers rarely seen elsewhere.

posts.title: Mesolithic timbers survive 10,500 years beneath a German lake
posts.dek: Worked posts and split boards found 20 metres underwater could rewrite what we know about hunter-gatherer construction in Central Europe.

posts.title: The Scouts at Ostia: A New Way to Bring the Ancient City to Its Neighbours
posts.dek: Around Ostia Antica the ancient city is swallowed by modern housing. A pilot project with a Scout Group tests whether community archaeology can work where no clear heritage community exists.
posts.source: Il capitale culturale. Studies on the Value of Cultural Heritage

posts.title: When the Neighbors Are the Community
posts.dek: A Scout Group steps into the role of heritage community at one of Rome's most urbanized archaeological sites, testing whether the concept can survive contact with a modern city.
posts.source: Il capitale culturale. Studies on the Value of Cultural Heritage

posts.title: A Scout Group as a Heritage Community
posts.dek: In one of Rome's most urbanized districts, a pilot project with a Scout Group tests whether community archaeology can work where no clear heritage community exists.
posts.source: Il capitale culturale. Studies on the Value of Cultural Heritage

posts.title: The shell that sent Lady 56 across medieval Europe
posts.dek: Ancient DNA separates the living from the dead at several medieval Swedish cemeteries. The burials were less about family ties, and more about community, custom, and possibly pilgrimage.

posts.title: The oldest complex cells were already choosing oxygen
posts.dek: More than 12,000 fossils from Australia link the earliest known eukaryotes to oxygenated seafloors between 1.7 and 1.4 billion years ago.

posts.title: A pyramid tomb where two worlds said goodbye
posts.dek: In Egypt's Western Desert, a small Roman-era pyramid tomb pairs hieroglyphic spells with a 19-line Greek poem for a man named Bisichthes.
